newsitem.title: SWEDEN: BA cargo prepares for Riga, Stockholm flights.
newsitem.headline: BA cargo prepares for Riga, Stockholm flights.

text.p: British Airways cargo division said on Monday the airline was preparing for the start of its London-Riga flights and an increase in capacity from Stockholm's Arlanda airport to its worldwide network.
From its summer timetable, British Airways will start flying London-Gatwick to Riga four times weekly using a Boeing 737 on Mondays, Wednesdays, Fridays and Sundays.

The airline will also double the frequency of its London-Heathrow to Stockholm operation from its present daily Boeing 767 operation. Containers prepared for a Boeing 767 would be compatible for a Boeing 747.
"With a twice-daily 767 we will be able to offer more direct services for larger consignments," British Airways World Cargo manager for northern Europe Anders Uddman told Reuters.
He said the air carrier was also preparing to start its first flights to the Baltic region, an area it believed had a lot of potential.
BA has been training personnel there because it did not plan to use its own staff, Uddman said.
Imports to the Baltic countries of Lativa, Lithuania and Estonia far exceeded exports, he said. Much of the countries' exports, like forestry products, were not goods generally shipped by air.
"Of the total volumes shipped to and from the Baltic region, probably 75 percent is import and 25 percent is export.

"For the future we believe there is potential because more and more companies are establishing themselves there and increased production means more air freight. That's why we're so keen to get out there," Uddman said.
